item.title: B O D Y | A poem by Mariyan Krachunov
item.description: Mariyan Krachunov’s debut poetry book is completed and will be published in the spring of 2026

item.title: B O D Y | Two poems by Stefan Ikoga, trans. Maria P. Vassileva
item.description: Stefan Ikoga is a multidisciplinary author who writes across poetry, prose, screenwriting, and advertising.

item.title: B O D Y | Two poems by Nadya Radulova, trans. Ekaterina Petrova
item.description: Nadya Radulova is a poet, fiction author, literary translator, and editor. She has authored six poetry books.

item.title: B O D Y | Three poems by Tom Phillips
item.description: Tom Phillips is a UK-born poet, translator and lecturer currently living in Bulgaria, where he teaches creative writing and translation at Sofia University.

item.title: B O D Y | A new poem by Peycho Kanev
item.description: Peycho Kanev is the author of 12 poetry collections and three chapbooks, published in the USA, Europe and India.

item.title: B O D Y | Three poems by Dimana Yordanova
item.description: Dimana Yordanova’s latest work, Letters to Niya, My Unborn Child, has been universally hailed as an important achievement.

item.title: B O D Y | A new poem by Ninko Kirilov
item.description: Ninko Kirilov is the author of books of prose, poetry and drama, most recently The Sun, The Heart (2025).

item.title: B O D Y | Five poems by Yanitsa Radeva, trans Drew Rollins
item.description: Yanitsa Radeva’s works have been translated into English, Korean, Macedonian, Romanian, Croatian, and Farsi.

item.title: B O D Y | Books in Brief: Four New Bulgarian Poetry Books in Translation
item.description: Drew Rollins and James Peake review four new books of contemporary Bulgarian poetry in translation. Edited by Clint Margrave.

item.description: Poet and translator Tom Phillips offers a guide to contemporary Bulgarian poetry in translation
